newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha highest in four years, trading quiet.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha highest in four years, trading quiet.

text.p: Naphtha prices hit a four-year high in afternoon Tokyo trade on Friday, in response to overnight crude gains, traders said.

First-half November open-spec naphtha was assessed at $207.00/$208.00, compared with late Thursday's $205.50/$207.50. Second-half November was bid at $206.50, while offers were notionally quoted at $207.50.
The levels are highest since June 1992, traders said.
However, trading remained mostly lacklustre as traders backed away from the market, carefully watching developments in the U.S.-Iraq conflict.
Naphtha spreads broadened further, with first-half November/first-half December nominally assessed at plus $1.00/$2.00.
In physical naphtha, petrochemical end-users in Japan are expected to start working on first-half November cargoes next week, with requirements for second-half October mostly satisfied, traders said.
Several South Korean end-users are still in search of second-half October lots, they added.
The Tokyo oil products market will be closed on Monday for a national holiday. -- Tokyo Commodities (81-3 3432 8837)
